page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by the AWS Graviton2 processor using ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture, configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs operating at 2.5 GHz without multithreading. Cache sizing includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions, 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not provide bundled local storage or hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results reveal balanced mid-tier execution for standard processing alongside modest performance in intensive synthetic benchmarks. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves average results with single-core and multi-core scores of 1519.39 and 6055.47, respectively. Large-block memory bandwidth measures 72.78 GB/sec for uncached reads and 35.07 GB/sec for writes, both falling within the middle 50% distribution. However, cached reads and Geekbench scores (961 single-core, 3217 multi-core) register in the lower 25%, while PassMark CPU and memory metrics show bottom-tier results. Database operations perform moderately at 2626.26 on PassMark, while Redis reaches 4.88 million SET operations per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, the absence of bundled local storage necessitates reliance on EBS network-attached storage, while the 6 Gbps network interface delivers steady baseline throughput for data transport. The dedicated single-threaded core architecture eliminates hyper-threading contention, yielding consistent per-thread runtime efficiency. The instance profile is suited for arm64-compatible network appliances, edge proxying, containerized microservices, CI/CD artifact building, and lightweight distributed web services that do not require heavy local storage or high per-core memory capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and driven by a 4-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on remote EBS volumes while maintaining a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the platform demonstrates middle-tier multi-core stress-ng throughput and solid uncached memory bandwidth, though instruction-heavy suites like Geekbench and PassMark reflect lower-tier compute scores. Featuring hardware AES cryptography and balanced networking capabilities, c6gn.xlarge is configured for arm64-native microservices, container routing, web server fleets, and lightweight backend services requiring dedicated core execution without large memory demands.
